transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2027-06-10 08:00 AM PT (15:00:00Z)
Duration: ~56 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recorded by: Fireflies
Links shared: benchmark_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx (link), security_addendum_v2.pdf (link), sample_trace_logs.tar.gz (link)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time this morning. quick agenda — run through the bench numbers, surface any regressions, routing playbook, and decide next steps. priya's got the data.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, dropping in the top-line: we ran three slices — small prompt, medium convo, and long-form summarization. compared against "IncumbentCloud" baseline. p50 is generally competitive, p95 still where we're seeing deltas on the long-form.
[01:05] Jordan (ProofPoint Eng Lead): can you define "competitive" here? like are we within 5 ms or 50 ms? our qa bar for p95 is pretty strict.
[01:22] Priya: yeah, good call. for the small prompt slice p50 is ~12ms vs incumbent 9ms, p95 is 42ms vs incumbent 28ms. medium convo p50 28ms vs 24ms, p95 78ms vs 52ms. long form p95 is where incumbent holds 120ms and we see 210ms in lab. so gap grows with kv cache misses and longer seqs.
[02:03] Maya (CTO): 210ms p95 on long form is a bit of a concern if that maps to user-visible latency. are we sure that's from KV cache churn and not a model or kernel mismatch?
[02:20] Priya: it's a mix. we saw two things — one is sequence-length dependent kernel choices in our runtime (we call out the fallback kernel), and second, our prefix cache hit rate for the dataset we used was only ~68% which increased the per-token cost. when cache hits are high p95 collapses to ~130ms.
[02:55] Ethan (SRE): what's the hit rate in production likely to be? our traffic has a lot of repeated prompts during form pre-fills — we'd expect higher cache hits.
[03:10] Jordan: yea our histogram is slightly spiky during some flows. i'll share a 72-hour trace.
[03:22] Alex: perfect, that helps. quick note on throughput — throughput numbers look strong. in our sustained load bench we delivered a 1.8x tokens/sec compared to incumbent when batching is allowed, but that came with 10-15% tail inflation on p95 for mixed traffic.
[03:50] Priya: to be precise: with adaptive batching enabled and a batch cap of 64 we saw 3400 tokens/sec sustained for the medium model vs incumbent ~1900 tokens/sec. with lower latency SLOs (batch cap 8) throughput falls to ~900 tokens/sec but p95 improves.
[04:18] Jordan: i'm thinking about real SLOs — we care about p95 for interactive, but also throughput for high-volume backfill jobs. do you recommend separate routing?
[04:36] Priya: yes, we generally route interactive traffic to low-latency pool (smaller batch cap, higher priority) and background jobs to dedicated high-throughput lane. Redwood's routing policy can do that — but that means you need two model variants pinned or different pool configs.
[05:05] Maya: what's the tradeoff on cost for two lanes? we have a firm budget.
[05:14] Alex: rough math — dual-lane adds ~25% unit cost vs single flexible lane but reduces SLA violations. however, with our smarter caching suggestions we expect to recoup 8-10% of that. we'll share the annotated sheet.
[05:40] Ethan: about the dedicated test — we want to run a 24h head-to-head. can you run Redwood in a dedicated slot so we avoid noisy neighbors?
[05:52] Priya: yes, we can provision a dedicated slot (that's Redwood Dedicated in the docs, sometimes called dedicated capacity) for the run. note that in the lab we used a shared pool which may explain a few of the tail events. dedicated run should tighten p95.
[06:23] Jordan: do we need VPC peering or can we hit it over public endpoints for the test?
[06:33] Alex: for short test it's ok to hit secure public endpoints with mTLS, but for realistic egress patterns and security scoping we'd recommend VPC peering. Ethan, i think your team will prefer peering.
[06:48] Ethan: yep we'll scope peering. i'll need firewall rules and the redwood egress ranges.
[07:00] Priya: i'll add that to the action items. on the kernel/quantization note — we tried int8 quantize for the medium model and saw a 12% latency improvement but some minor tokenization differences on highly specific legal prompts. your QA team flagged two hallucination-like outputs.
[07:28] Maya: that's worrying — our clinical content is sensitive. we can't accept any drop in generation quality without manual review. what are the options?
[07:41] Priya: you can keep the full-precision variant for high-sensitivity flows and use quantized model for low-risk workloads. Redwood Optimize also suggests per-route quantization profiles. quantization is reversible in our deployment so you can A/B it.
[08:05] Jordan: can we get a per-prompt quality checklist? our reviewers need concrete metrics not just "minor differences".
[08:18] Alex: we can share the eval prompt set and a simple regressions table showing top-5 diffs. will attach in the spreadsheet.
[08:38] (crosstalk, brief)
[09:05] Priya: back to routing — fallback policy: when the low-latency pool is constrained we can fall back to a slightly higher-latency but cheaper model. important detail: fallback increases p95 for those requests by ~30-50ms in our tests.
[09:33] Jordan: that seems tolerable for some flows but not for our auth flows. we need an allowlist.
[09:42] Priya: absolutely — route by endpoint and by token type, you can pin flows. we'll show how to map endpoints to routes in the config.
[10:08] Alex: security — Maya, you asked about SOC2 and KMS. i've uploaded the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration doc. short version: Redwood supports customer-managed keys and HSM-backed KMS in private deployments; for hosted we support envelope encryption and we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account roles.
[10:36] Maya: one more question — audit logs retention. we need 1 year with exportable CSVs.
[10:44] Alex: that's available as an add-on; we'll include pricing in the estimate.
[11:02] Ethan: latency variance — any idea if the variance we saw is reproducible under different instance types? our ops perf team prefers GPU type A but we tested type B in the lab.
[11:18] Priya: yes, kernel selection and memory bandwidth matter. we used A100-equivalent but not the exact same vendor hardware as your prod. dedicated run can match your target instance. we'll coordinate.
[11:40] Jordan: OK let's recap the blockers which might explain the p95 gap: 1) lower prefix cache hit in lab dataset, 2) shared pool noise in lab, 3) kernel mismatch. if we fix those three in a dedicated head-to-head we expect p95 to come down close to incumbent. is that accurate?
[12:00] Priya: that's our hypothesis. also tuning batch caps by traffic slice and enabling smarter prefix caching based on your traffic should close more of the gap.
[12:16] Maya: timeline for the dedicated test?
[12:20] Alex: we can schedule the dedicated 24h slot as early as next week — provisioning and peering setup takes 2-3 business days. so week of 2027-06-21 is realistic.
[12:40] Jordan: that works. after the run we'll want a write-up comparing p50/p95 and a sample of outputs for quality vetting.
[12:52] Priya: we'll produce an annotated report and include raw traces and the tuned routing config.
[13:08] Alex: pricing — quick estimate for the dedicated slot + one-time test is included in the pricing doc i'll share; pilot extension pricing options also in the sheet.
[13:22] Jordan: any mention of competitor differences that are worth calling out? the incumbent is using a heavier batching approach and has some ASIC optimizations, LexiconAI claims lower p95 on certain seq lengths but at higher unit cost.
[13:45] Priya: yeah incumbent's ASIC/stack gives them an advantage on long seqs. our strength is more flexible routing, caching, and better unit economics if you adopt dual-lane routing.
[14:05] Maya: final question on compliance — can Redwood Private be deployed into our VPC for the pilot if needed?
[14:16] Alex: yes, Redwood Private (private control plane) or our on-prem package can be scoped; that's heavier lift and usually reserved for later-stage enterprise adoption. for the head-to-head we recommend peering into a dedicated slot first.
[14:36] Jordan: sounds good.
[14:50] (brief pause)
[15:05] Priya: ok i'll summarize the technical tasks in the sheet. one note — we saw a specific outlier event at 2027-06-04 18:03 UTC that coincides with a background backfill in the lab; might be noisy neighbor. we'll mark that.
[15:28] Ethan: i'll double-check our backfill windows and avoid them during the dedicated run.
[15:40] Alex: excellent. next steps recap — redwood sends annotated sheet and security addendum by 06-13, ProofPoint shares 72h trace by 06-16, PIR for dedicated slot week of 06-21.
[16:00] Jordan: cool. any other questions?
[16:08] Maya: none from me. thanks everyone.
[16:15] Alex: thanks — we'll follow up in email and slack with scheduling links.

End of transcript.
